classification.difficultyReason: Substitute a line equation into a circle equation, solve the resulting quadratic and recover the corresponding coordinates, including a repeated root and fractional coordinates.

content.prompt: Find the points of intersection of:

answer.worked:
From the line, $y=\dfrac{25-4x}{3}$. Substitute into the circle:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+\left(\frac{25-4x}{3}\right)^2&=25\\9x^2+(25-4x)^2&=225\\9x^2+625-200x+16x^2&=225\\25x^2-200x+400&=0\\x^2-8x+16&=0\\(x-4)^2&=0\\x&=4.
\end{align*}$$
Then
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac{25-4(4)}{3}\\y&=3.
\end{align*}$$
There is one point of intersection, $(4,3)$.

Substitute $y=3x-1$ into the circle:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+(3x-1)^2&=29\\x^2+9x^2-6x+1&=29\\10x^2-6x-28&=0\\5x^2-3x-14&=0\\(5x+7)(x-2)&=0\\x&=-\frac75\text{ or }2.
\end{align*}$$
When $x=-\dfrac75$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=3\left(-\frac75\right)-1\\y&=-\frac{26}5.
\end{align*}$$
When $x=2$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=3(2)-1\\y&=5.
\end{align*}$$
The points of intersection are $\left(-\dfrac75,-\dfrac{26}5\right)$ and $(2,5)$.
